title: K2: integration-owner key and REGISTER TEST REF (host-local registry, owner-only)
outcome: An operator-written integration-owner key {sessionId, sessionCreationId} is loaded, reloaded on change and exposed read-only with source path and SHA-256, and an owner-only REGISTER TEST REF operation records a durable registration row (item, ref, commit, tree, clean-checkout schema-1 fingerprint, named-root content-v1, expected platform(s), optional required toolchain, registering identity, instance, time) after verifying the named root clean at the commit.
acceptance: Tests show the key loads at start and reloads on change with its hash and time logged, is exposed read-only with source path and SHA-256, and that registration by any caller other than the configured owner is refused with integration_owner_unset or integration_owner_identity_mismatch.

Tests show a registration verifies the item's named root is clean at the given commit, persists the full row in the persisted state (serde-default, no schema bump), refuses re-registering the same ref to a different commit, and retires the row on deletion; each refusal is named and records nothing.
The full gate passes on the exact final input that lands, with an independent review pair and no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding on that input.
disposal_reason: Superseded by the automatic remote-result design (Greg, Advisor #2639; Fable2 #4079): no operator owner key, REGISTER TEST REF or registration registry.
